mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months, it signals monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in non-farm payrolls indicate a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC for interaction term falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), rising consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and RSAFS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (index 2017=100) for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction, signaling economic weakness and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in housing starts below 1000 thousand units for two consecutive months indicates weakening residential demand, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation monetary regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rising federal funds rate signals aggressive tightening that increases borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
